scope: User stories for Justin's root page, reusable personal PR templates, and future client design pitches.

personas.name: Recruiter or hiring manager
personas.description: Needs a fast trust read and a direct path to resume, proof, and contact without reading a long bio.

personas.name: Potential collaborator
personas.description: Wants to understand what Justin makes, how he thinks, and whether there is a natural route into deeper work.

personas.name: Personal visitor
personas.description: Arrives from social or search and wants a normal, curated human read without private material being exposed.

personas.name: Client or small business prospect
personas.description: Needs to decide whether this person or template system feels organized, tasteful, and credible enough to contact.

personas.name: Template operator
personas.description: Uses the platform to turn a reusable design direction into a governed client template without hand-copying design decisions.

stories.story: As a recruiter, I want to understand the person and reach resume or proof in a few seconds so that I can decide whether to keep evaluating.
stories.why: Hiring visitors will not read a manifesto before checking credibility.
success_criteria: The first mobile screen exposes identity plus at least two professional exits.
Resume and proof routes are visually obvious without a visible pitch headline.
No route label or URL changes are required to understand the next step.
anti_goals: A marketing hero that explains value props.
A dense resume wall on the root.
template_implications: Keep professional exits high in the visual hierarchy.
Prefer object labels and route affordances over paragraphs.
Use mobile spacing as the default constraint.

stories.story: As a collaborator, I want a quick sense of projects, docs, and thinking so that I can find the right deeper surface to explore.
stories.why: Collaboration starts from evidence of taste, range, and working style.
success_criteria: Docs and code exits are findable without reading category explanations.
The site creates curiosity without hiding the useful routes.
Future project modules can be added without rewriting shared content.
anti_goals: Generic categories such as work, systems, or experiments as the main signal.
A portfolio grid that depends on unready content.
template_implications: Support route objects that can become project or docs modules later.
Keep shared content universal and template-owned layout separate.
Make room for a garden/docs surface without forcing it into the root.

stories.story: As a personal visitor, I want the site to feel like a real person with taste and boundaries so that I trust the public identity without seeing private life.
stories.why: The root should be a curated glimpse into life, not a raw feed or private archive.
success_criteria: Personal texture is opt-in and public-reviewed.
The first impression feels normal and alive, not like a tech stack identity.
Social exits are present without dominating professional routes.
anti_goals: Private photos, locations, feeds, or direct-link details.
A page that performs being personal through excessive copy.
template_implications: Keep privacy review gates in the contract.
Let visual grouping and interaction do more work than visible headings.

stories.story: As a client or small business prospect, I want to see a tasteful, flexible template system so that I can imagine adapting it to my own public identity.
stories.why: The product should scale beyond Justin without flattening every client into one generic template.
success_criteria: The design system can explain its fonts, palette, modules, and motion in a readable one-pager.
Each candidate template is a full alternate design, not a spacing tweak.
Template selection can happen without changing canonical content.
anti_goals: One-off CSS with no design objects.
A template that only works for a software developer.
template_implications: Require bibliography, user stories, requirements, pitch, one-pager, design objects, tokens, and build plan before implementation.
Keep template-specific presentation in template folders.
Use source IDs so design rationale can be audited.

stories.story: As a template operator, I want agents to read contracts, sources, stories, objects, and tokens before building so that autonomous slices remain governed.
stories.why: Agentic work needs machine-readable constraints or design changes drift into taste-only patches.
success_criteria: Validation fails when a pitch references missing bibliography, user-story, or requirement IDs.
Build plans keep implementation slices tied to approved sources.
Generated templates stay inactive until preview and screenshot review.
anti_goals: Manual reconciliation branches for missing metadata.
Agents guessing the design basis from prose.
template_implications: Extend validator coverage to research and story artifacts.
Update execplan templates to require research inputs.
Keep JSON as source of truth and Markdown as readable output.
